headline: US stocks set to open modestly higher near record levels as earnings momentum continues and oil firms on Iran-linked geopolitical tensions
raw_text:
- S&P 500 (@ES), Dow Jones (@YM), and Nasdaq 100 (@NQ) futures trade modestly higher, pointing to a gap-up open that keeps US equities near all-time highs as earnings momentum persists
- Low-float names RAIN (RAIN), ENSC (ENSC), and ELPW (ELPW) post outsized pre-market gains on thin volume driven by news-related catalysts
- Larger pre-market movers include Palantir (PLTR), DXST (DXST), Intel (INTC), and First Solar (FSLR) trading notably higher ahead of the open, while Aon (AON) and Zimmer Biomet (ZBH) hold flat
- Semiconductor and memory stocks such as Micron (MU) show mixed pre-market action, with some names up modestly and others down sharply
- SpaceX (SPCX) is in focus ahead of its first public earnings report after the bell, with shares reacting modestly following a post-IPO decline
- Early checks show no major US earnings beats or misses reported before the bell
- Today’s US data docket features the trade balance at 8:30 AM ET, followed by factory orders and JOLTS job openings at 10:00 AM ET
- European equities trade higher, with the DAX and FTSE 100 supported by strength in BP (BP) and miners
- BP (BP) reports Q2 profits at their highest level in four years, supported by elevated oil prices partly linked to developments involving Iran
- Crude oil (@CL) prices remain firmer as ongoing geopolitical tensions continue to underpin the energy complex, while Asian markets trade mixed with some strength in India
